## Function to update an estimate of a 1-inflated beta distributed mean

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)
library()
```

```{r syntheticData}


# I will simulate som data and test the wgt_mean function
n <- 1000

tempDF <- tibble(
  # first, some population samples with different properties
  uniform = runif(n, 0, 1),
  normal_centered = rnorm(n, 0.5, 0.2),
  normal_high = rnorm(n, 1, .5),
  beta_2_2 = rbeta(n, 2, 2),
  beta_05_3 = rbeta(n, .5, 3),
  beta_3_05 = rbeta(n, 3, .5),
  # add some area weights
  wgt = seq(1:n)
) |>
  # truncate
  mutate(across(
    !starts_with("wgt"),
    ~ case_when(
      . >= 1 ~ 1 #0.9999,  using pmin and pmax is another option
      . <= 0 ~ 0 #0.00001,
      .default = .
    )
  )) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = !starts_with("wgt"),
    names_to = "distribution",
    values_to = "population_sample"
  ) |>
  nest(population_sample = population_sample, wgt = wgt) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
  # get the shape parameters
    # this step has been moved into the function itself.
  #     shape1 = EnvStats::ebeta(unlist(population_sample))$parameters["shape1"],
  #     shape2 = EnvStats::ebeta(unlist(population_sample))$parameters["shape2"],
    # they are quite close to the original shape parameters
    # simulating samples using a beta distribution, trying to recreate the original population samples
    #simulated_sample = list(rbeta(n, shape1, shape2)),
    
    # creating some test cases of domain samples, 
    
    # 1's
    domain_1a = rep(1,2), # 2 1's in a row
    domain_1b = rep(1,5), # 5 1's in a row
    domain_1c = rep(1,10), # 10 1's in a row
    domain_1d = rep(1,30), # 30 1's in a row
    
    #  high values
    domain_2a = seq.int(0.8, 1, length.out=2),
    domain_2b = seq.int(0.8, 1, length.out=5),
    domain_2c = seq.int(0.8, 1, length.out=10),
    domain_2d = seq.int(0.8, 1, length.out=30),
    
    #  low values (further from the population shape)
    domain_3a = seq.int(0.1, 0.4, length.out=2),
    domain_3b = seq.int(0.1, 0.4, length.out=5),
    domain_3c = seq.int(0.1, 0.4, length.out=10),
    domain_3d = seq.int(0.1, 0.4, length.out=30),
    
    # truncated normal
    domain_4c = rnorm(10, 1, .5) |> pmin(1) |> pmax(0),
    domain_4d = rnorm(30, 1, .5) |> pmin(1) |> pmax(0),
    
    
    # get posterior distributions
    PD_1 = list(
      wgt_mean(
        x = unlist(population_sample)[1],
        weights = unlist(wgt)[1],
        shape1 = shape1,
        shape2 = shape2
      )
    ),
    PD_2 = list(
      wgt_mean(
        x = unlist(population_sample)[1:2],
        weights = unlist(wgt)[1:2],
        shape1 = shape1,
        shape2 = shape2
      )
    ),
    PD_5 = list(
      wgt_mean(
        x = unlist(population_sample)[1:5],
        weights = unlist(wgt)[1:5],
        shape1 = shape1,
        shape2 = shape2
      )
    ),
    PD_10 = list(
      wgt_mean(
        x = unlist(population_sample)[1:10],
        weights = unlist(wgt)[1:10],
        shape1 = shape1,
        shape2 = shape2
      )
    ),
    # and weighted sample means
    wgt_mean_1 =
      wgt_mean(
        x = unlist(population_sample)[1],
        weights = unlist(wgt)[1],
        shape1 = shape1,
        shape2 = shape2,
        stat = "mean"
      ),
    wgt_mean_2 =
      wgt_mean(
        x = unlist(population_sample)[1:2],
        weights = unlist(wgt)[1:2],
        shape1 = shape1,
        shape2 = shape2,
        stat = "mean"
      ),
    wgt_mean_5 =
      wgt_mean(
        x = unlist(population_sample)[1:5],
        weights = unlist(wgt)[1:5],
        shape1 = shape1,
        shape2 = shape2,
        stat = "mean"
      ),
    wgt_mean_10 =
      wgt_mean(
        x = unlist(population_sample)[1:10],
        weights = unlist(wgt)[1:10],
        shape1 = shape1,
        shape2 = shape2,
        stat = "mean"
      ),
    # adding the PD means
    posterior_mean_1 =
      mean(unlist(PD_1)),
    posterior_mean_2 =
      mean(unlist(PD_2)),
    posterior_mean_5 =
      mean(unlist(PD_5)),
    posterior_mean_10 =
      mean(unlist(PD_10)),
    # adding the samples
    sample_1 =
      list(unname(unlist(population_sample)[1])),
    sample_2 =
      list(unname(unlist(population_sample)[1:2])),
    sample_5 =
      list(unname(unlist(population_sample)[1:5])),
    sample_10 =
      list(unname(unlist(population_sample)[1:10])),
    # adding unweighted sample means
    mean_1 = mean(sample_1),
    mean_2 = mean(sample_2),
    mean_5 = mean(sample_5),
    mean_10 = mean(sample_10)
  )
```

```{r }
set.seed(123)
national_data <- c(
  rnorm(1000, mean = 0.8, sd = 0.1) %>% pmax(0) %>% pmin(1), # Truncated normal
  rep(1, 200) # 1-inflation
)
x <- national_data
x_trunc <- x[x > 0 & x < 1]

#MASS::fitdistr(x_trunc, dbeta, start = list(shape1 = 1, shape2 = 1))$estimate
#EnvStats::ebeta(x_trunc)$parameters

fit_zoib <- function(x) {
  prop_1 <- mean(x == 1)
  prop_0 <- mean(x == 0)
  x_trunc <- x[x > 0 & x < 1]
  alpha <- MASS::fitdistr(x_trunc, dbeta, start = list(shape1 = 1, shape2 = 1))$estimate
  list(alpha = alpha, prop_1 = prop_1, prop_0 = prop_0)
}

national_fit <- fit_zoib(national_data)

mean(national_data)
hist(national_data)
mean(national_data == 1)
```
